summary.intent: Bootstrap release-please with proper tags to clean up an excessive changelog (PR #427), align api-client versions with the API, and test the release system with a quick task adding version to the /health endpoint.
summary.outcome: Successfully created 15 bootstrap tags, aligned api-client versions to 0.35.0, fixed OpenAPI spec generation to use dynamic versioning, added version to /health endpoint, and got the release-please system producing clean changelogs. PR #429 merged with all review comments resolved.

repo: Release-please treats entire commit history as unreleased when no prior tags exist — bootstrap tags must be created manually on a known SHA before the release system can generate clean changelogs.
The manifest at .release-please-manifest.json tracks 15 packages across apps/, packages/, and crates/ directories.

HealthController is excluded from the OpenApiGeneratorModule (generate-openapi.ts:102-114) because it depends on TypeOrmHealthIndicator which requires a live DB connection — instead there is a manually-defined health spec in the same script.

Phase 41 discussion log (41-DISCUSSION-LOG.md:106) explicitly decided monotonic (major.minor) versioning for web and desktop apps, but implementation defaulted to semver. Decision was deferred — semver acceptable for now.
The pr-release-preview.js script processed merge commits as regular commits, causing false release label generation. GitHub PR commits API returns parents array; merge commits have 2+ parents.
Using fix: commit type triggers patch version bumps via release-please — internal/CI fixes should use chore(ci): to avoid unnecessary version churn.
npm_package_version env var is not reliably set in all execution contexts; reading package.json directly with fs.readFileSync is the safer fallback pattern for the API.
openapi.json is regenerated by orval from the spec; the generate-openapi.ts script manually defines the health endpoint schema since it cannot be auto-generated.

code.finding: Originally used hardcoded '0.1.0' for OpenAPI version; fixed to read from npm_package_version env var with fs.readFileSync package.json fallback.
Same hardcoded '0.1.0' issue; fixed with fail-fast pattern if env var missing.

Health endpoint is manually defined in the spec here because HealthController cannot be instantiated without TypeORM. The version property was missing from the manual schema definition and had to be added explicitly.
Merge commit filtering added here — skip commits where parents.length >= 2 to avoid false release label triggers from merge commits.
openapi.json added as an extra-file with jsonpath pattern for the apps/api package so release-please bumps the version field in the generated spec automatically on release.

workflow: Bootstrap tags for release-please should be created on the last known stable commit (before the release tooling was added), not HEAD, to avoid including setup commits in the first changelog.
Squashing commits before force-push to rewrite commit type (fix: → chore:) is the correct approach to prevent unintended release-please version bumps.
The GSD quick task workflow can be interrupted mid-executor to override commit message conventions — executor can be skipped and implementation done directly with correct commit scope.
Running pnpm api:generate after merging release commits can produce formatting-only churn in openapi.json due to JSON serialization differences — safe to batch with next meaningful change.

friction: Cargo.lock regeneration pulled in unrelated dependency updates when cargo update was run — had to restore original and use targeted workspace-only update instead.
Auto-merge showed as enabled in the GitHub UI but gh pr view returned autoMergeRequest: null, causing confusion about merge status.
The GSD executor was spawned before the user could specify the commit message convention (feat(api): vs generic message) — had to interrupt and implement manually.
npm_package_version unreliability was flagged by both Copilot and CodeRabbit as separate review threads on the same underlying issue, requiring two separate fixes and reply/resolve cycles.
openapi.json formatting churn after api:generate made it unclear whether there were real changes to commit — required diffing to confirm it was whitespace-only.
open_items: Phase 41 decision to use monotonic (major.minor) versioning for web and desktop apps was deferred — currently using semver. Revisit if versioning semantics matter later.
15 bootstrap tags were created to clean up the initial changelog, but the release-please system is brand new — first real release cycle will validate whether the workflow is solid end-to-end.

The health endpoint version field is manually maintained in generate-openapi.ts schema definition — if the HealthController is ever refactored to not require TypeORM at instantiation time, it could be included in the auto-generated spec instead.
